title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Service of Judicial Documents in Foreign-Related Civil or Commercial Cases

articles.content_en: Article 1 When a People's Court tries a foreign-related civil or commercial case, these Provisions shall apply to the service of judicial documents on a person to be served who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 2 The "judicial documents" as mentioned in these Provisions refer to copies of the statement of complaint, copies of the statement of appeal, copies of the statement of counterclaim, copies of the statement of defense, summons, judgments, mediation agreements, rulings, orders for payment, decisions, notices, certificates, proofs of service, and other judicial documents.

Article 3 Where the natural person who is the person to be served, or the legal representative or principal person in charge of an enterprise or other organization, is within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may serve on the natural person or the legal representative or principal person in charge.

Article 4 Unless the person to be served has clearly stated in the power of attorney that the litigation agent has no authority to receive the relevant judicial documents on his or her behalf, the entrusted litigation agent shall be the litigation agent who has the authority to accept service on behalf of the person to be served as provided in item (4) of Article 267 of the Civil Procedure Law, and the People's Court may serve on the litigation agent.

Article 5 When serving judicial documents on a person to be served, the People's Court may serve them on a representative office established by the person to be served within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
Where the person to be served has a branch office or a business agent within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may, upon authorization by the person to be served, serve on the branch office or business agent.

Article 6 When a People's Court serves judicial documents on a person to be served who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, if the country where the person to be served is located has concluded a judicial assistance agreement with the People's Republic of China, service may be effected in the manner prescribed by the judicial assistance agreement; if the country where the person to be served is located is a member state of the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, service may be effected in the manner prescribed by that Convention.
Where service is effected in the manner prescribed by an international treaty concluded or jointly acceded to by the country where the person to be served is located and the People's Republic of China, it shall be handled pursuant to the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Handling Requests for Judicial Assistance in the Service of Judicial Documents and the Taking of Evidence in Civil and Commercial Cases Pursuant to International Conventions and Bilateral Judicial Assistance Treaties.

Article 7 Where judicial documents are served in accordance with a judicial assistance agreement, the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, or through diplomatic channels, if six months have elapsed from the date on which the relevant organ of the People's Republic of China transmitted the judicial documents to the relevant organ of the country where the person to be served is located, and no proof of service or non-service has been received, and it cannot be determined on the basis of the circumstances that service has been effected, service by that method shall be deemed impossible.

Article 8 If the country where the person to be served is located permits service by mail, the People's Court may serve by mail.
When serving by mail, a proof of service shall be enclosed. If the person to be served fails to sign for receipt on the proof of service but signs the postal receipt, service shall be deemed effected, and the date of signing shall be the date of service.
If three months have elapsed from the date of mailing, and no proof of service or non-service has been received, and it cannot be determined on the basis of the circumstances that service has been effected, service by mail shall be deemed impossible.

Article 9 Where the People's Court serves by public announcement pursuant to item (8) of Article 267 of the Civil Procedure Law, the content of the announcement shall be published in newspapers and periodicals publicly distributed domestically and abroad.

Article 10 In addition to the service methods provided in the preceding articles of these Provisions, the People's Court may serve the person to be served by other appropriate means that can confirm receipt, such as facsimile or electronic mail.

Article 11 In addition to service by public announcement, the People's Court may simultaneously adopt multiple methods to serve the person to be served, but the date of service shall be determined according to the method by which service is first effected.

Article 12 When serving judicial documents on the legal representative, principal person in charge, litigation agent, representative office, or the branch office or business agent authorized to accept service of the person to be served within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may apply the method of service by leaving the documents at the place of service.

Article 14 Where, in accordance with relevant provisions, judicial documents need to be transmitted through the higher-level people's court, the People's Court shall attach a letter applying for transmission.
Upon receiving the judicial documents submitted by the lower-level people's court for transmission, the higher-level people's court shall transmit them within seven working days.
Where the higher-level people's court considers that the judicial documents submitted by the lower-level people's court for transmission do not comply with relevant provisions and need to be corrected, it shall return them to the people's court that applied for transmission within seven working days.

Article 15 Where, in accordance with relevant provisions, a translated version needs to be provided for the service of judicial documents, the People's Court accepting the case shall entrust a translation institution within the territory of the People's Republic of China to make the translation.
The translated version shall not be affixed with the seal of the People's Court, but shall be signed or sealed by the translation institution or translator to certify that the translation is consistent with the original.
Article 16 These Provisions shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
